message.content:
Lion (Panthera leo) and zebra (Equus zebra) belong to two different orders—Carnivora and Perissodactyla, respectively.  
Their most recent common ancestor is the last common ancestor of the **Laurasiatheria** super‑order, a placental mammal that lived roughly 90–100 million years ago. This ancestor would have been a small, generalized mammal that gave rise to the diverse lineages that eventually became the modern cats and horses.

So both are in Laurasiatheria. The last common ancestor of Carnivora and Perissodactyla is the last common ancestor of the clade Laurasiatheria. So the common ancestor is the last common ancestor of Laurasiatheria. That would be a mammal that lived around 90-100 million years ago. So the answer: the last common ancestor of the Laurasiatheria clade, which is a placental mammal that lived about 90-100 million years ago. Alternatively, we can say the common ancestor is the last common ancestor of the superorder Laurasiatheria, which is a mammal that lived around 90-100 million years ago.
